submitted.rationale: Index 2 (Bi0.22 Cu0.30 V0.48) gave the highest measured photocurrent, 44.7 µA. XRD shows monoclinic BiVO4 (Q≈2.03) plus a secondary phase (Q 1.746, likely a Cu vanadate). This two-phase mix outperforms Cu-poor BiVO4 (index 7, 1.24 µA). Index 4, one step further toward Cu, has the same phases but was lower (37.3 µA), which puts the optimum near index 2.

rejected.reason: Measured 1.24 µA: Cu-poor BiVO4 lacks the secondary phase and is 36x weaker.
Measured 37.3 µA: same phases as index 2 but lower photocurrent.
XRD shows the Q 1.746 phase is replaced by a different phase (Q 1.48); not measured.
Bi-rich and multiphase by XRD; unlikely to beat the V-rich region.

consultations.verdict: Weak support. According to MEGNet, the Bi and V binary oxides have gaps of 2.3–2.8 eV, which 3.2 eV light can excite. CuO's gap is only 0.3 eV, which is metallic-like and likely to cause recombination. That favours the Bi/V-rich, Cu-poor region, where BiVO4, a 2.4 eV photoanode, is expected to form. Index 7 (Bi0.40 Cu0.19 V0.41) has Bi:V≈1 and near-minimum Cu, so I'm measuring it first.

Mildly supportive, but mostly uninformative. The V-oxide gap (2.1–2.8 eV) is below 3.2 eV, so V-rich compositions absorb the illumination. XRD shows index 2 is BiVO4 plus a secondary phase (probably a Cu vanadate), which could form a heterojunction. Measuring it tests the V-rich/Cu-richer side against index 7.

The Cu-oxide gap is small (about 1.3–1.6 eV), so adding more Cu risks recombination centres. That argues for staying within the BiVO4 + Cu-vanadate two-phase field rather than pushing into Cu-rich regions. XRD shows index 4 has the same phases as the high-photocurrent index 2 (Q 1.746 phase present), while index 41 moves into a different assemblage. Overall this supports measuring index 4.
